input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: new venture stormwater-detention-sizer (NRCS hydrographs, level-pool routing, two-stage outlet sizing)
errors: First draft skipped weir sizing when the orifice alone held the large storm, over-detaining (6.50 ft basin vs 5.33 ft); caught on reviewing the sample output, fixed before commit.
README Spec-sources line first read 'Signed off by a licensed civil engineer', which nobody has done; reworded to 'would sign this off ... none has yet' before commit.

doc_friction.issue: Runs the test command inside the venture dir, so a repo-root test path fails the baseline; the hint explains it, but the PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK example doesn't say so.

deviations.why: 'Calculators are a poor use of a run': built a new tool anyway, because it is a routing engine with a two-stage design search (an iterative simulation a chatbot cannot do reliably in one reply), on the owner's construction direction, filling a gap next to earthwork-cut-fill.
deviations.did: New venture with engine, page, guide, CLI and tests
deviations.result: Landed with 27 venture tests, 4/4 mutants caught

notes: Explore idea: stormwater detention pond sizer (construction direction). NRCS CN runoff + triangular UH + alternating-block storm from IDF + storage-indication routing with bisection + orifice/weir sized by bisection. Checked by hand calcs, linear-reservoir exact solution, mass balance, independent RK4 (0.5%). Not checked against HydroCAD/HEC-HMS: next step is a published routed example. No agent doc: the README and post carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a water-resources engineer writing and testing a routing and two-stage sizing engine plus page and guide

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
